summary: This Dockerfile creates an Ubuntu container with git, zsh, and fzf installed, then sets up a demo git repository scenario with a feature branch in progress and uncommitted changes. It also installs a custom zsh function called `gwt` that uses fzf to interactively navigate between git worktrees, and configures the shell prompt to indicate we're in a container.

explanations.3: This tells the installer to skip interactive prompts during package installation, letting commands run without waiting for user input.
explanations.7: The ubuntu docker image doesn't enable all software repositories by default; this command adds the 'universe' and 'multiverse' repositories so packages like fzf become available to install.
explanations.15: After installing packages, we delete apt's cache files to reduce the final image size, since we won't need to install anything else.
explanations.29: This creates nested directories in one go (with -p flag) so we can organize our demo project structure before initializing git.
explanations.71: This uses awk to extract the first field (the directory path) from the selected worktree line; the funky quoting escapes the single quotes so they survive being written to a file.
explanations.75: This constructs the worktree directory path by taking the repository root and appending the branch name with slashes converted to dashes (so feature/user-notifications becomes feature-user-notifications).
explanations.87: The >> operator appends these lines to the existing .zshrc file instead of overwriting it, so previous configuration isn't lost.
explanations.94: This makes the container start an interactive login shell by default when it runs, so you get a prompt to type commands into.
